incidents.rule: Read an environment file line by line, never shell-source it; a value with angle brackets breaks sourcing
incidents.signature: The runbook failed at its first step on a value the shell parsed as syntax.

incidents.title: A registry edit failed its own sorted-order assertion, and the identity checker refuses a supersession whose old path the registry still names
incidents.rule: Change the registry line and the supersession record whose old path it names in one control commit, and assert the sorted order first
incidents.signature: A registry edit and a supersession record conflicted when landed separately.

incidents.title: A reviewer finding moved a hook registration owner twice in one hour
incidents.rule: Assign a hook registration owner only after reading which row owns the hook's neighbours
incidents.signature: The owner of one registration changed twice in about an hour.

incidents.title: A closure packet freeze test turned positive on a control-only landing and the lead admitted it narrowly
incidents.rule: Admit a freeze-test hit only narrowly: name the landing, why the run cannot read it, and the change that makes it a new STOP; never waive the identity step
incidents.signature: A freeze test reported a change that the guarded run could not read.

incidents.title: A scoped compiler config flagged an import style that the canonical build never compiles
incidents.rule: Check a scoped compiler diagnostic against the canonical build before calling it a defect; fix a scoped-config artifact in the retained config, not the repository
incidents.signature: A scoped compile failed on a file the canonical build does not compile.

incidents.title: A review was reassigned off the critical path so the reviewer who owned the blocking recheck stayed on it
incidents.rule: Keep the reviewer on the critical path on that path and reassign off-path reviews to another non-author
incidents.signature: One reviewer held two reviews while a blocking recheck waited.

incidents.title: A captions upload relation in a spec would have added a media referrer to a collection defined as image-only
incidents.rule: Before adding a relation to a shared collection, check what the collection holds and which referrer lists it joins; defer and record a gap if it does not fit
incidents.signature: A relation targeted a collection that does not accept its content.

incidents.title: A framework operation order showed that file data is generated before the field validators, so a security check moved to the operation hook
incidents.rule: Place a security check on original input in a hook that runs before the framework transforms the input, verified in the installed source, and record any move as a named deviation
incidents.signature: A content check ran after the framework had already rewritten the input it was meant to inspect.

incidents.title: A generated migration needed a lint-only edit, so the evidence carries the raw and delivered hashes and the one-line diff
incidents.rule: When a generated file needs a lint-only edit, change only the named defect and record the raw hash, the delivered hash and the diff
incidents.signature: A generated file failed lint while its content was correct.

incidents.title: A host load spike came from operating system daemons, not the team, and the load wait held
incidents.rule: A load gate holds regardless of who causes the load; continue static work and do not touch system daemons
incidents.signature: Host load was far above the gate while no team run was active.

incidents.title: A supersession marker was deferred to each row's activation because writing it now would trip the freeze test
incidents.rule: Defer a marker or registry change that would trip an active freeze test to the activation step, and name the approval it will cite
incidents.signature: A control write was due while a freeze condition forbade control changes.

incidents.title: A dependency question was answered by the backlog itself, a relation owned by a later row, so no wait was needed
incidents.rule: Before waiting on a dependency, read the backlog for the row that owns it; if a later row owns it, ship without it and add no stub
incidents.signature: A spec raised a wait on something a later row was already scheduled to add.

incidents.title: A route validator rejected a width that the generator was required to emit
incidents.rule: Check every producer output against every consumer validator before signing a design, with a control for the edge output and for each refused value
incidents.signature: A consumer refused a value that its own producer was required to emit.

incidents.title: Interim content was signed as clearly marked placeholder copy instead of being invented as sourced
incidents.rule: Sign interim content as a visibly marked placeholder with its open question and owner; never present an invented value as sourced
incidents.signature: Seed content needed text that no source provided.

incidents.title: Hand delivery under a hold, with one reconciliation after the load, replaced blocking on a state flip
incidents.rule: Under a held state flip, deliver by hand on the established precedent and reconcile once after the hold; keep every freeze rule
incidents.signature: Three rows waited on a backlog state flip that was held on purpose.

incidents.title: A job text swapped two commit identities, and reading the log caught it
incidents.rule: Read the log for every commit a job text names before acting on it, and record the correction
incidents.signature: Two commits were named the wrong way round in an instruction.

incidents.title: A reviewer's framework claim was corrected from the installed source: a draft save writes only the versions table
incidents.rule: Verify a reviewer's framework claim in the installed source before adopting it, and cite the source
incidents.signature: A reviewer stated a framework behavior that the installed source does not show.

incidents.title: A low-load window needed immediate dispatch of the gated runs
incidents.rule: When a low-load window opens, dispatch the gated runs at once, reading the load in its own command before each launch
incidents.signature: Gated runs waited while a short low-load window was open.

incidents.title: A squash recipe equated the landing tree with a stale branch tree and would have dropped later main work
incidents.rule: A squash landing tree must equal the merge result of the pinned main and the branch head, never the branch tree; rebuild when main moves
incidents.signature: A landing recipe that would have silently removed work already on main.

incidents.title: Evidence receipts leaked absolute paths into branch history, and the lead landed by squash instead of rewriting history
incidents.rule: Write evidence commands with placeholders for paths and tools; handle leaked history by a squash landing that keeps the original branch as the local audit trail
incidents.signature: The leak guard reported absolute paths and a tool name inside evidence files.

incidents.title: A lint rule against a throw inside a finally block caught a real defect in production code
incidents.rule: Treat a lint error as a defect: restructure, pin each intended behavior with a unit case, and add no disable comment or rule change
incidents.signature: A final lint gate failed on code that looked finished.

incidents.title: A generated down migration dropped a table with cascade and then dropped the removed constraint again
incidents.rule: Fix a generated down migration by a minimal named edit with raw and delivered hashes, and report it as static until a round trip proves it
incidents.signature: A down migration contained a statement that fails after an earlier statement had already removed its target.

incidents.title: An image library throw on undecodable bytes surfaced as a server error instead of a refusal
incidents.rule: Catch a library throw on untrusted input and refuse with a client error status and a stable reason code; pin it with a valid-signature, bad-body case
incidents.signature: Malformed upload bytes produced a server error.

incidents.title: A geometry spec's rounded intermediate broke a test tolerance, caught by independent arithmetic
incidents.rule: Recompute spec geometry independently against the oracle tolerance, round at the last step, and never loosen the oracle
incidents.signature: A spec's numbers did not meet the test tolerance they were written for.

incidents.title: The lead wrote a ruling timestamp before reading the clock
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing each timestamp; write the time after the read, not before
incidents.signature: A ruling carried a time written before the clock was read.

incidents.title: A self-imposed freeze outlived its reason and was blocking three rows' activations
incidents.rule: Re-derive a freeze's mechanism before honoring it; withdraw it when the guarded run cannot read what it protects
incidents.signature: A STOP kept blocking work after the run it protected could no longer be affected.

incidents.title: A static closure packet that did not converge in three rounds was replaced by running the thing and diagnosing the receipts
incidents.rule: When a static closure packet does not converge in three rounds, replace it by running the thing on current code and diagnosing the receipts
incidents.signature: Static review rounds kept finding the same open items.

incidents.title: A migration lock covered the whole branch when it needed to cover only the generators and schema paths
incidents.rule: Scope a lock to the shared paths and commands it protects, not the whole branch, and state how a second branch rejoins after the holder merges
incidents.signature: A second branch idled although most of its work did not touch the locked resource.

incidents.title: A fresh worktree can be provisioned by a copy-on-write clone of the dependency tree instead of an install that may hit dead store links
incidents.rule: Provision a fresh worktree by a copy-on-write clone of the dependency tree, never by linking, when an install may hit dead store links
incidents.signature: An offline install failed on dead links in the package store.

incidents.title: Tests authored but never executed passed acceptance, and the first run of the heavy tier found a failing case
incidents.rule: Accept a production merge only after the heavy test tier passes on the merged tree; authored but unexecuted cases are missing evidence, not a pass
incidents.signature: A row was signed off with part of its tests never run.

incidents.title: Two fields mapping to one database enum made the generated migration narrow a five-state status to two states
incidents.rule: Give each field that persists a state set its own enum name per table, and check the generated SQL for every state before generating types
incidents.signature: A generated migration silently narrowed a status to fewer states than the field allows.

incidents.title: The lead missed six teammate replies across a context compaction and left the critical-path engineer idle for 35 minutes
incidents.rule: Check thread activity right after every context compaction, before any other step
incidents.signature: Replies sat unread after a compaction.

incidents.title: A load gate stop was the right call and cost nothing because the runner created nothing before the check
incidents.rule: Put the load check before anything is created, so a gate stop costs nothing and leaves nothing to tear down
incidents.signature: A run stopped at the gate while the host was overloaded.

incidents.title: The lead missed eight teammate replies with no compaction and saw them only through thread activity
incidents.rule: Check thread states after every landing batch, not only after a context compaction
incidents.signature: Replies were missing from the lead view while the work sat finished.

incidents.title: A ruling cannot override a teammate tool rules, so the lead sleep loop load waiter was refused and withdrawn
incidents.rule: Wait for load with an event driven observer owned by the lead, never a sleep loop in a teammate; a ruling does not override a teammate tool rules
incidents.signature: A ruled helper was refused by the teammate it was meant for.

incidents.title: Teammates cannot remove or drop, so teardown belongs to the lead and runs from the runner names file
incidents.rule: Plan teardown as a lead owned step driven from the runner names file, and keep walk pass and cleanup pass separate
incidents.signature: Cleanup could not be run by the teammate that created the things.

incidents.title: A file creation mask from an earlier tool call did not carry over, and the database dump came out world readable
incidents.rule: Set the mask, run, and assert the result in one command, because shell state does not carry across tool calls
incidents.signature: A dump file was readable by others for a short time.

incidents.title: A provenance check that the generator can never satisfy: the zero parent id on every snapshot
incidents.rule: Prove a diff base from what the generated SQL does and does not emit, and never demand a check the generator can not satisfy
incidents.signature: A required check was impossible to pass whatever the code did.

incidents.title: The lead wrote ruling timestamps from memory three times and had to correct them
incidents.rule: Compute a timestamp from the clock in the same command that writes it, never from memory
incidents.signature: Timestamps in rulings were wrong until corrected.

incidents.title: A ruling wrote a media directory binding from memory that contradicted the pinned scripts, and the runner stopped instead of substituting
incidents.rule: Check a binding against the pinned scripts before writing it, and stop on a contradiction rather than substitute
incidents.signature: A written binding contradicted the scripts it was meant to drive.

incidents.title: A generated down migration defect fixed once came back in the next row because the fix was never turned into a check
incidents.rule: Turn a fixed generator defect into a check on the list that every later generated migration runs
incidents.signature: A defect already fixed once appeared again with no check to catch it.

incidents.title: A new required argument broke an older direct caller that the change did not list
incidents.rule: When an argument becomes required, list every direct caller, tests included, and keep the old call path or update every caller in the same change
incidents.signature: A whole unit run showed one more failure after a signature change.

incidents.title: An order sensitive comparison of two tool listings failed only when new files were added, though the contract was set membership
incidents.rule: Compare sorted copies when the contract is set membership, and keep order sensitive equality for contracts that define order
incidents.signature: A test failed after unrelated files were added.

incidents.title: A hook ran a query on create with an undefined id once a registry became non empty: a latent defect exposed by data, not code
incidents.rule: Guard a hook query on the operation and a valid id; a check over an empty population proves nothing about the non empty case
incidents.signature: A seed failed with a database type error after a data change.

incidents.title: An identity guard compared to a plain address while the database cast rendered the address with a mask, so it could never pass, and a silent catch hid which check failed
incidents.rule: Probe a guard against the real value it will see; a guard that can never pass is a defect, and a catch must print which step failed without secrets
incidents.signature: A walk stopped at its helper with one generic error.

incidents.title: A subprocess call failed with not found when the pinned runtime directory was missing from the search path, and the first run showed five extra failures
incidents.rule: Put the pinned runtime directory on the search path in the same command that runs the tests; a not found error from a spawned tool is an environment fault, not a product failure
incidents.signature: Extra failures appeared in the first run.

incidents.title: Color escape codes in a report broke an extraction assertion, and only the zero match assertion caught it
incidents.rule: Strip terminal escape codes before parsing a report, and keep a zero match assertion so a failed extraction writes nothing
incidents.signature: An extraction found no matches in a report that held the text.

incidents.title: An admission sent at a low load reading reached the runner after the load rose again, and the runner fresh reading then refused it
incidents.rule: An admission admits the step: a reading within 60 seconds of the admission is a record, and a reading after that is a fresh gate
incidents.signature: A runner refused a step that had just been admitted.

incidents.title: A script carried internal load vetoes that contradicted a later decision, and the script bytes were immutable
incidents.rule: When a ruling changes a gate, list every script that encodes the old gate before the ruling is relied on
incidents.signature: A script stopped a run on a gate that a ruling had removed.

incidents.title: A run plan barred the test author from running the script, and a later message assigned that author anyway
incidents.rule: Check an assignment against the independence rules of the plan before sending it
incidents.signature: A message contradicted the plan it was meant to follow.

incidents.title: A helper finished its work but hung in the framework shutdown call, and its pass line came after the shutdown, so no evidence printed
incidents.rule: Write the evidence line before any shutdown call, bound the shutdown with a timeout, and exit explicitly
incidents.signature: A step did its work and then sat idle with no output.

incidents.title: A long acceptance run launched with a detached command inside a subshell from a tool shell never started, and no output file existed minutes later
incidents.rule: Launch a long run as a tracked background task, and check that its first output file exists right after the launch
incidents.signature: A launched run left no output and no process.

incidents.title: A count change in an acceptance document was attributed to specific items without a per file check
incidents.rule: State a count delta with its base commit, and attribute it to a row only after a per file check
incidents.signature: A count change was credited to rows with no per file evidence.

incidents.title: Drafts proposed test database ports by reading tracked text, and two clashed with each other and two with live listeners
incidents.rule: Allocate shared numbered resources centrally and probe the live system at use time; a text search for free numbers is not a probe
incidents.signature: Proposed numbers collided with each other and with live listeners.

incidents.title: The first browser test to load the app config failed to link because one module was reached by two loaders
incidents.rule: Reproduce a loader failure with minimal variants before editing product code, and keep modules shared with the app config graph out of static import chains that a test runner compiles differently
incidents.signature: A module that exports a name was reported as lacking it.

incidents.title: A test file was edited on order although its digest was pinned by the test authors, and the integrity gate refused the run before it started
incidents.rule: Before ordering an edit to a test file, check whether a digest manifest pins it; if it does, route the change through a successor version authored by a test author, not a direct edit.
incidents.signature: An ordered test edit made the integrity gate refuse the run before it started.

incidents.title: A whitespace check over the branch range failed on generated SQL, while the same check on the working tree alone had passed
incidents.rule: A worktree only whitespace check is not range proof; run the check over the branch range, exclude generator output by path, never reformat it, and keep every other path clean.
incidents.signature: A worktree only check passed where the branch range check failed.

incidents.title: A process guard stopped a run twice: the listing was padded with trailing spaces, and the guard's own command line matched its search
incidents.rule: A process guard normalises only trailing whitespace in process list output and searches with a self excluding pattern in a call that contains nothing else; it keeps failing closed.
incidents.signature: A guard that searches the process list failed on padding and on matching itself.

incidents.title: Unit mutation testing on a merged change found two survivors while every named test passed
incidents.rule: A passing suite is not a discriminating suite; run cheap mutations before merge, count only runs that executed the tests, and open a follow-up change for survivors instead of reopening the merge.
incidents.signature: Mutated code passed the whole suite.

incidents.title: A browser test failed at its first request, and after that was fixed the next run failed at a step that had never run
incidents.rule: When a fix moves a failure later in a test, treat every newly reached step as never verified; a green earlier step proves only that step.
incidents.signature: Fixing an early test failure exposed a later step that had never run.

incidents.title: A guard that blocked every network attempt logged only the API name, so a second run was needed to learn the target
incidents.rule: A blocking guard logs the API name, the full arguments and a stack trace on the first run, so one run is enough to classify the target.
incidents.signature: A blocking guard recorded what was called but not where.

incidents.title: A leak scanner that walked the working directory reported an ignored local file, and the push gate blocked on a file that never ships
incidents.rule: Gate a push on a scan of an export of the tracked tree; a scan of the working directory blocks on files that never ship.
incidents.signature: A scan of the working directory flagged a file outside the pushed tree.

incidents.title: A push gate that piped the test run into a trimming command would have pushed even if the tests had failed
incidents.rule: Never pipe a gating command; capture its exit status first, by pipefail or by writing to a file and checking the status before reading the file.
incidents.signature: A gating command was piped, so the gate read the last command status.

incidents.title: Two new work item ids were minted from the current list alone, and both had already been used by merged work
incidents.rule: Before minting an id, check every place ids have ever lived (branch names, commit subjects, plan text), not only the current list; a checker that reads only the current list cannot catch reuse.
incidents.signature: A checker that read only the current list passed ids that history had already used.

incidents.title: Tests added by a branch were never run before the merge, and the full suite failed on them afterwards
incidents.rule: Before a merge, the branch acceptance run must run every test file the branch adds or changes, in its own test group; a full run after the merge is a backstop, not the first execution.
incidents.signature: Tests nobody ran before the merge failed on their first execution after it.

incidents.title: A test counted a whole shared directory, and the reset reseeded into it
incidents.rule: A test that counts a shared directory or table must count only what the case creates, by baseline delta or by name, because the per-test reset and seed change the total.
incidents.signature: A total taken over a shared directory included files the case did not create.

incidents.title: A test fixture failed an earlier check than the one under test
incidents.rule: Build a fixture that passes every guard except the one under test, and assert which guard refused; an earlier guard's refusal masks the guard the case is meant to prove.
incidents.signature: The case failed on the wrong guard, so the intended guard never ran.

incidents.title: A merge checklist drafted early found a test change the merge would have broken
incidents.rule: Draft the merge acceptance checklist while the row is still open, and for each source change read the tests that assert on it, so owed test changes are found before the merge turns the full run red.
incidents.signature: A source change altered a seed record, while a unit test still asserted the old shape.

incidents.title: An approval on main was not an ancestor of the branch that needed it
incidents.rule: An approval that landed on main after a branch forked is not an ancestor of that branch; merge main into the branch before any activation commit that a checker ties to that approval.
incidents.signature: A checker required the approval commit to be an ancestor of the branch head, and the branch had forked before the approval landed.

incidents.title: A setting that strips tokens from responses also stripped them from the test helper
incidents.rule: When a security setting strips tokens from responses, it strips them from local test helpers too; capture the token before the response is sanitized and assert it is present, or every downstream auth check fails at its precondition and looks like a product defect.
incidents.signature: Every auth check downstream of a local login failed, and the token was empty at the first step.

incidents.title: Static review rounds on a test harness left the same findings open
incidents.rule: When static review rounds on a harness converge slowly, run one labelled diagnostic early, on scratch state, with its result marked as neither a baseline nor an acceptance run, to learn what is really wrong.
incidents.signature: Two static passes ended with the same four findings still open.

incidents.title: A rule written in teammate briefs was broken by the lead in its own shell
incidents.rule: A rule written in teammate briefs binds the lead's own shell too; read your own command against the standing rules before running it, and undo any slip by its exact recorded name before any run.
incidents.signature: The author of a standing rule broke it by reflex while setting up a new work tree.

incidents.title: A wrapper exited zero while a step record said the step failed
incidents.rule: Gate on the step records, never on the wrapper exit status; a wrapper can exit zero while a step record says failed.
incidents.signature: The wrapper exit status was zero and one step record said failed by timeout.

incidents.title: A browser walker gathered guards over many static rounds until no allowed target could pass them
incidents.rule: When a test tool's guards are reviewed in more rounds than the tool is run, run it or simplify it; a guard that no allowed target can pass is a defect.
incidents.signature: A diagnostic run packet showed the tool could not run against any allowed target.

incidents.title: A successor test root was named so the identity checker could never accept it as a successor
incidents.rule: Name a successor after the family it supersedes, and read the checker's acceptance rule before writing the mapping; never loosen the gate to fit the artifact.
incidents.signature: The successor carried a name from a different family than the root it replaced.

incidents.title: An order named a scratch target without reading the guard of the command that would fill it
incidents.rule: Before naming a target in an order, read the guards of every command you name against that target.
incidents.signature: The target named in the order was on the list of targets the named command refuses.

incidents.title: The first real click-around found product defects that many static review rounds and every gate had missed
incidents.rule: Run the real product early and often; a cheap exploratory run beats another review round of the tool that would run it.
incidents.signature: A cheap exploratory run on a real build produced mismatches on every checklist row, within an hour of parking the strict tool.

incidents.title: The acceptance run lacked an environment variable that the branch run and the full suite set
incidents.rule: Record the environment of every run you compare, and give the acceptance run the same environment the full suite gives.
incidents.signature: The only new failure in the acceptance run was a test that throws when one environment variable is absent.

incidents.title: An acceptance record was ready for signature with every test tier green while the main page of the row was blank
incidents.rule: Before signing a row that ships a page, require one observed run of that page; green test tiers alone are not acceptance for a user-facing row.
incidents.signature: Every test tier was green and a page the row ships returned a blank body.

incidents.title: A flag that hides the token from responses left first-user registration with an empty session cookie
incidents.rule: When a change hides or removes a credential from responses, test every flow that needs that credential to finish, not only that it is hidden.
incidents.signature: Registration returned success and stored the admin, and the browser landed on the login page.

incidents.title: The first browser run of new end-to-end cases found two product defects that config reads and other tiers missed
incidents.rule: A config that lists a column or a field is not evidence that the page shows it or works offline; only a browser run on the real page is.
incidents.signature: A config listed a column and a field, and the real page showed neither as intended.

incidents.title: The first defect of a kind prompted an audit of the whole kind, which found a second
incidents.rule: When one instance of a defect class appears, audit for the whole class before fixing only the instance.
incidents.signature: One hard-coded external host was found in a page that must work offline, and a second, silent one existed on the server.

incidents.title: One load gate sized for full runs was applied to every run, and scoped runs were refused while the real load producer went unexamined
incidents.rule: Size an admission gate to the class of run it protects, and find what is actually producing the load before tightening or waiting on it.
incidents.signature: A single load threshold chosen for full-suite runs refuses small scoped runs once several teammates work in parallel.

incidents.title: An error named only the leaf of an import chain, and a rule to add a link only when the next run named it spent a run per link
incidents.rule: When an error names only the leaf of a dependency chain, trace the chain in source and act on all of it, rather than letting each run name the next link.
incidents.signature: A load error names one package, but that package is reached through others that fail the same way.

incidents.title: An implementer was assigned after checking only who wrote the test payload, and the root also held a coverage statement the implementer had written
incidents.rule: An author-conflict check covers every file of the root, including coverage statements and approval markers, by log and a name search, before the assignment is sent; the implementer own check stays as the second line.
incidents.signature: An author-conflict check was run on one file of a root, and a different file of the same root named the assignee as author.

incidents.title: A brief stated a baseline environment from a compacted summary, and the baseline script showed the opposite
incidents.rule: State a baseline environment from the script or log that produced it, never from memory; an implementer who sees a premise contradict the artifact follows the artifact and reports it.
incidents.signature: A brief says a baseline ran with a variable unset, and the script that produced the baseline sets it.

incidents.title: A branch scrubbed a local path in a later commit, and a range scan found it still in history
incidents.rule: Scan every commit of a range, not only the final tree, before merging anything that will be pushed; a scrub in a later commit does not clean history.
incidents.signature: The final tree passes a leak scan, and a scan of every commit of the range does not.

incidents.title: A run command silently dropped a named option, and three tests that ran it asserted only things that are true for the full data set too
incidents.rule: A test that exercises an option goes through the real entry point and asserts an observable effect that differs with and without the option; exit 0 and side markers are not evidence the option took effect.
incidents.signature: A test runs a command with an option and asserts exit status, timing and a side marker, all of which hold with or without the option.

incidents.title: Two fields claimed the same publication state, and the seed wrote only one, so the admin and the public predicate disagreed
incidents.rule: When two fields can claim one state, derive one from the other or assert both in the same test, and write through the framework supported transition.
incidents.signature: An application status says published and the framework draft status says draft for the same record.

incidents.title: An independence rule did not say what counts as an agent or as a part, and four of nine parallel slices stopped at once
incidents.rule: Define independence per agent instance, and name which artifacts block (wrote the test or judged its cases) and which only need disclosure (inventories, citation audits).
incidents.signature: A rule says to stop if you authored or reviewed any part, and different agents read part and agent differently.

incidents.title: A build step was given the load threshold meant for timing-sensitive runs and was refused twice while the host was busy
incidents.rule: Pick each step load threshold by whether its result depends on timing; a build that only gets slower uses the looser class.
incidents.signature: A strict admission threshold designed for timing-sensitive runs is applied to a step whose result does not depend on timing.

incidents.title: An agent reported a background run as running from its launch, but the task had only echoed a prompt and no test process existed
incidents.rule: Report a run as running only from its own output (a launch line, a PID that exists); a started task is not a started run.
incidents.signature: A background task exists and a launch was acknowledged, but no process of the run exists.

incidents.title: Mutation restore receipts were kept only in tool output, so two independent reviewers could not verify restoration
incidents.rule: A mutation run keeps a receipt per mutant, the diff and the hash after restore, as a file before the scratch copy is deleted; tool output is not evidence a second reviewer can check.
incidents.signature: A reviewer asks for proof that a mutated file was restored, and the only record is output that was not saved.

incidents.title: A harness test failed because another run's orphan database vanished mid-test, so the test depended on state it did not own
incidents.rule: A test must not assert on state it did not create; compare only the names the test itself made.
incidents.signature: A cleanliness assertion over a shared server sees a resource disappear between its baseline and its end.

incidents.title: Read-once-and-refuse load admission stopped whole teammate cycles while load spiked and fell within a minute
incidents.rule: When load is spiky, admit by waiting for the gate with a bounded timeout and a printed admitting reading, not by one reading at launch.
incidents.signature: A launch is refused on one load reading, and the next reading a minute later would have admitted it.

incidents.title: An activation moved a superseded root's spec while main carried the approved successor edge, and identity failed only after the merge
incidents.rule: Before activating a root, confirm on current main that it is still the terminal of its supersession chain; run the identity check after merging main into the branch, not only before.
incidents.signature: An identity check reports a missing deletion of a pending copy after a branch merges a main that supersedes the activated revision.

incidents.title: An implementer proposed editing a pinned root's mock to fit a new helper contract, and the fix was a wrapper that kept the mocked shape
incidents.rule: When a new contract collides with a pinned test mock, keep the mocked function return shape and add a new function or wrapper for the new contract; change the test only through a successor root authored by someone else.
incidents.signature: A new return contract is incompatible with a pinned test's mock, and the proposed fix edits the pinned file.

incidents.title: A rulings file grew past what a reader's tool returns, and a read of a named range was clipped, so compliance could not be certified
incidents.rule: Do not require a read whose size exceeds what the reader tool returns; name the exact sections to read, and treat an unnamed old section as outside the compliance check.
incidents.signature: An instruction requires reading a range of a file whose size exceeds what the reader tool returns.

incidents.title: Backlog rows stayed open after their fixes merged, so the backlog no longer showed what was done
incidents.rule: Update a backlog row status with the merge commit at the time its fix merges, so the backlog stays the record of what is done.
incidents.signature: The backlog lists as open rows whose fixes are already on the main line.

incidents.title: Two reviewers were named who had written or judged the roots they were to review, and both stopped at the author check
incidents.rule: Before naming a reviewer, read the root coverage author line and review history; the reviewer own author check is the second line, not the first.
incidents.signature: A reviewer is named without reading the root author line and review history, and the reviewer author check refuses.

incidents.title: A landing tool read a bare file name as a test-root name, so a file was left out of a landing and the identifier check failed
incidents.rule: A tool that accepts both root names and file paths must not guess which one a bare token is; list what it will land and compare with what was intended before it runs.
incidents.signature: A tool accepts root names and file paths, and a bare file name is taken as a root name.

incidents.title: A root was passed to a landing helper by name and by path, and the cleanup removed a file twice and stopped
incidents.rule: Give a landing helper each item once and in its one documented form; an item named twice is a cleanup that can fail halfway.
incidents.signature: The same item is given to a helper in two forms, and a later step acts on it twice.

incidents.title: A manifest listed its lines unsorted and the landing gate refused it
incidents.rule: Run the landing gate own identity check on a root before handing it over, so a mechanical ordering rule is met by the author and not found at the landing.
incidents.signature: The identity check requires sorted manifest lines, and a manifest lists one group before another.

incidents.title: Three unit tests timed out at a short child-process bound under parallel load and passed in isolation
incidents.rule: A short child-process bound fails under parallel load while the test is correct; classify such a timeout by an isolated rerun, and give child-process tests a bound that tolerates the load class they run in.
incidents.signature: Tests that spawn a child process fail with a spawn timeout at a five-second bound only while the host is loaded.

incidents.title: A helper script was edited in place while another process was executing it, and that run died with a syntax error at a shifted line
incidents.rule: Never rewrite a script in place while any process may run it; write a new file and switch names, and quote the helper hash in the evidence that used it.
incidents.signature: A script that other threads run is rewritten in place, and a running shell fails at a line number that no longer matches.

incidents.title: Three test roots by three authors used the same guessed locator for a generated field that the installed library does not render
incidents.rule: Do not guess a locator for a generated field; cite the installed source line that renders it, and when one guess is found, audit every root for the same guess.
incidents.signature: Several browser tests scope a generated field by a role or label that its library never renders.

incidents.title: A root named a mutation its assertions could not see, because the next line returned the same status
incidents.rule: A mutation named as a case witness must be one the assertions can see; trace what the next line returns before naming it, and state the expected red line.
incidents.signature: The named mutation is removed, and the case still passes because a later line refuses the same way.

incidents.title: A feedback check accepted any visible alert on the page, so a stale alert could satisfy it
incidents.rule: A feedback assertion must fail without the action under test: assert the element is absent before the action and present after it, on a fresh page and scoped to the field, never on any alert on the page.
incidents.signature: An assertion looks for any visible alert, and an alert from earlier or from another field satisfies it.

incidents.title: A reviewer was named after checking commit authorship only, and the reviewer had judged the root's cases in an earlier review file
incidents.rule: An author-conflict check covers review files as well as commits: search both for the root identifier and read the author of every hit before the reviewer is named.
incidents.signature: An author-conflict check covers commits, and the conflict is in a review file.

incidents.title: An absence check for a hidden field matched the hidden input the library renders, so a regression root was red on unchanged code
incidents.rule: A regression root must be green on unchanged code before any mutation; an absence selector for a hidden field must account for the hidden input the library still renders.
incidents.signature: A test asserts that a selector for a hidden field matches nothing, and the library renders a hidden input with the field id.

incidents.title: A fix gave a list column a custom cell and dropped the default cell's link to the record, so the list lost its only way to open a record
incidents.rule: Replacing a framework default cell, field or component replaces everything it did, not only what the change targeted; list what the default provided before replacing it, and test it.
incidents.signature: A custom cell component replaces the default cell, and the default cell carried the record link.

incidents.title: A full run stopped at the unit step because one test hit the runner's default five-second bound while host load rose sevenfold
incidents.rule: A per-test bound left at the runner default is a decision nobody made; set it at the project level for the load class the step runs in, and treat a default-bound timeout under load as a wasted run, not a red.
incidents.signature: A unit test fails with a timeout at the runner's default bound, and the host load at the end of the step is many times that at its start.

incidents.title: An icon-only button had no accessible name, so a role-name locator could never match and the test timed out
incidents.rule: Before writing a role-name locator for a control, read the installed source for its accessible name; an icon-only control with no label has none, and a test that waits for one can only time out.
incidents.signature: A test waits for a button by role and name, and the button has no name to match.

incidents.title: A graceful pause worked because each in-flight teammate finished one step, wrote a checkpoint and left its workspace as it was
incidents.rule: To pause a team safely, tell each in-flight teammate to finish only the current step, write a resume checkpoint, and leave its worktree and processes as they are; resume from those checkpoints and never redo finished work.
incidents.signature: A team stops on request and resumes later, and every member continues from its own recorded state.

incidents.title: Test roots imported helpers by paths anchored at their pending depth, so every import would break at the active destination
incidents.rule: Check that every import of a root resolves from the path where the file will run, not only from where it is written; a pending copy that must move byte-identical cannot be repaired at activation.
incidents.signature: A spec imports by relative paths that resolve from its pending folder and climb outside the repository from its active folder.

incidents.title: A named mutant was masked by an independent guard upstream, so the case could never turn red for the stated reason
incidents.rule: Before naming a mutation as a case witness, trace every independent guard on the path from the mutated line to the assertion; a second guard masks the mutant.
incidents.signature: A mutation weakens one access setting, and a separate guard on the same path still refuses.

incidents.title: A configuration mutation failed a setup assertion before any case oracle ran, so the red proved nothing about the cases
incidents.rule: A mutation counts for a case only when it fails at that case own assertion; check that the setup and fixture assertions do not fail first.
incidents.signature: A mutation breaks the configuration, and the shared setup asserts the same configuration and fails first.

incidents.title: A standing promise to guard every proven behavior had no inventory, so partial protection could pass as coverage
incidents.rule: Turn a broad protection promise into a per-item inventory with strict status definitions, a count, and a proposed guard for every gap; partial protection of a row is a gap.
incidents.signature: A broad request such as never break what already works is acknowledged but never turned into a per-item count of what is guarded.

incidents.title: A one-line comment conflict hid a type break from the automatic part of the merge
incidents.rule: After any merge conflict, inspect the whole merged file for changes the tool resolved automatically and run the type check before accepting; a tester does not resolve product conflicts.
incidents.signature: A merge conflict looks like one stale comment, while the automatically merged lines of the same file are inconsistent with each other.

incidents.title: A protection root pinned an exact seed inventory, and a feature row that grew the seed turned it red
incidents.rule: A root that pins an exact inventory should derive it from the source declarations and fail closed on a shape change; a right-reason red from legitimate growth is fixed by a reviewed successor, never by the implementer editing the test.
incidents.signature: An active root asserts an exact count of seeded records, and a feature branch adds more records.

incidents.title: A dispatch draft marked every unsourced value for the lead to bind instead of guessing
incidents.rule: When a value is missing, mark it for the owner to bind and list the gap; never fill it with a precedent or a guess.
incidents.signature: A packet contains values with no source in any record, such as a credential location, a clock setting or a build mode.

incidents.title: Two reviewers in a row were assigned a slice they had already worked on, because the pick did not search the record
incidents.rule: Before assigning a reviewer, search the record for every earlier author or judge of the row and pass the findings to the reviewer.
incidents.signature: A reviewer is picked from availability alone and then stops at the author check.

incidents.title: A successor root needed to change a file owned by another row family, and the identity checker allows replacement only within one family
incidents.rule: When a change touches files owned by different row families, plan one successor per family; do not widen the checker or add a cross-family marker.
incidents.signature: One successor root must edit a file that a different row family owns.

incidents.title: A reviewer accepted an initial red that only proved a new function was missing, and said so
incidents.rule: An initial red that only shows a new function is missing is not behavioral evidence; say so, and ask for a mutation or old-code run that reaches the behavioral assertions.
incidents.signature: A test-first red fails on an assertion that the new function exists.

incidents.title: A mutation that flipped a field-level unique flag was masked by a unique index the migration had already created
incidents.rule: When a rule is enforced in the schema as well as in code, a right-reason mutation must defeat both layers, in a disposable database with an exact recorded name.
incidents.signature: The mutated product setting is not the only thing enforcing the rule, because a database index enforces it too.

incidents.title: Before two origins shared one production build, the engineer searched the build output for the baked origin and found none
incidents.rule: Before reusing one production build for several origins, search the build output for the baked origin and record the empty result.
incidents.signature: A production build can embed an origin or address, which would make one build wrong for a second origin.

incidents.title: A walk load limit was unreachable because the host floor without any team job sat above it
incidents.rule: Measure the host load floor with no team job before fixing an admission limit; if the floor is above it, use the documented scoped limit and serialize the other runtime jobs.
incidents.signature: A wait-for-load limit is below the idle load of the host, so every admission would wait forever.

incidents.title: A landing helper guessed the kind of each argument from its shape, so a plain file name was read as a pending root
incidents.rule: A helper must not guess whether an argument is a path or a name; take an explicit kind or fail closed on an unknown bare word.
incidents.signature: A helper treats any word without a slash or a leading underscore as a name of a kind, not as a file.

incidents.title: A reviewer asked for a mutant to run with a case filter, but the row runner takes one row and no filter
incidents.rule: When a runner cannot filter cases, run the whole row and attribute each red to its own case line; never credit another case baseline red as a kill.
incidents.signature: A review note names a run option that the runner does not have.

incidents.title: A walker harness could not open a blank autosave draft from the list because its name link had no text, and a second selector matched three links
incidents.rule: Reuse the exact recorded link instead of a looser selector, and record the element evidence for a link that cannot be clicked.
incidents.signature: A list link has no accessible text, and a looser selector matches more than the one intended link.

incidents.title: An activator could not recover an earlier brief mutant text, so it named its own mutant and said so
incidents.rule: If an assigned mutant cannot be recovered, name your own, say so, and record its diff and restore hash; put mutant text in a file, not only in a message.
incidents.signature: The brief that carried the mutant text is no longer available to the activator.

incidents.title: A reviewer wrote its own browser-only driver to reach a mutant after the row runner stopped at an integration red, without asking
incidents.rule: When a mutant needs only part of a row, ask the lead first; do not write a private driver, and run every restored green through the standard runner.
incidents.signature: The standard runner cannot reach the part of a row a mutant needs, and the runner is replaced by an ad hoc script.

incidents.title: Integration files that need a live server failed with connection refused under a runner that starts none, first read as a branch regression
incidents.rule: Before reading a red as a regression, run the same files with the same runner on the main branch; a connection refused under a runner that starts no server is a precondition, not a regression.
incidents.signature: Tests fail with connection refused on a branch, and the cause is a missing precondition of the runner.

incidents.title: A test that passed alone at about 63 percent of its timeout budget timed out in a loaded whole-suite run
incidents.rule: A test that needs over half its timeout budget alone will time out under load; raise the budget with the measured duration recorded, and do not touch the assertion.
incidents.signature: A test finishes at well over half of its budget alone, then times out under load.

incidents.title: The walker helper produced two provisional mismatches of its own, which it traced and corrected append-only before any defect was filed
incidents.rule: Trace a provisional mismatch to its expectation before filing a defect, and correct it append-only with evidence.
incidents.signature: A walk check reports a mismatch that comes from the helper expectation, not from the product.

incidents.title: A proposal found that the product itself writes the state a fixture needed, which turned a validation-bypass question into a product path
incidents.rule: Before bypassing validation for a fixture, look for a product path that writes the state; if none works, stop and report rather than fall back to SQL.
incidents.signature: A fixture needs a record that normal validation would refuse, which suggests bypassing validation.

incidents.title: A host-wide load gate held a one-shot, time-windowed check until its window passed, because processes outside the team drove the load
incidents.rule: Do not let one host-wide load threshold admit every job alike: size the gate to the job, attribute the load to its owners first, and reserve capacity for any observation that has a deadline.
incidents.signature: Every runtime job, from a full suite to one read-only browser check, waits for the same host one-minute load average to fall under a fixed limit, while processes the team does not own set that load.

incidents.title: A load average of 176 was read as CPU demand while no process used more than one core, because the number counts waiting work and lags
incidents.rule: Before acting on a high load average, list the top processes by CPU with their owners; a load far above the core count with no process above one core is waiting work or lag, not CPU demand.
incidents.signature: A one-minute load average far above the core count while the per-process CPU list shows no process above one core.

incidents.title: A polling host lock does not serve waiters in order, so a test run queued after its own setup took the lock first and failed on a database setup had not created
incidents.rule: Never rely on start order across separate acquisitions of a polling lock; run dependent steps under one acquisition or use a first-come ticket lock.
incidents.signature: Two dependent steps are queued as separate acquisitions of a lock that waiters poll for, and the later one runs first.

incidents.title: The lock holder waited for the load to fall while still holding the host lock, and eleven agents fed that one lock, so waits of 20 minutes became normal
incidents.rule: Never hold a shared lock while waiting on a condition that other waiters also need, and match the number of agents doing runtime work to the capacity of the serialized resource, not to the size of the team.
incidents.signature: Recorded lock waits grow with the number of agents, while the lock holder itself is waiting on the load gate.

incidents.title: Two agents cancelled their queued heavy jobs by task id during a pause, but the queued shells survived; one later took the host lock and ran its test after the agent had reported it cancelled
incidents.rule: A cancellation is complete only when the job's own PIDs are gone from ps; record that check in the checkpoint, and make any helper that waits on a lock exit when its parent dies.
incidents.signature: A job reported as cancelled has a log whose first line is written after the cancellation time, or its shell PIDs still answer ps.

incidents.title: A successor root was authored and approved without a run, and its first baseline failed because the installed config had one more internal collection than its exact list
incidents.rule: A root that pins a list of framework internals must be checked against the installed configuration and run once before approval; a setup failure is a root defect, fixed by a new successor, never by an in-place edit.
incidents.signature: An exact list of framework internals in a root is stale against the installed configuration.

incidents.title: A mutant made the product raise its own domain error inside the awaited expectation, before the matcher ran, and the agent disclosed that it was not an assertion error
incidents.rule: Classify a non-assertion red by where it was raised: a domain error from the mutated path inside the expectation is a right-reason kill; setup, timeout, harness or outside-path errors are not.
incidents.signature: A red whose error type is not an assertion error, raised by the mutated product path.

incidents.title: A verifier matched plain text in colored logs and stopped
incidents.rule: Strip color escapes for matching only; never alter the raw evidence bytes or the hash of them.
incidents.signature: A text match over raw logs that contain terminal color escape codes.

incidents.title: The first real run of a new egress observer on unchanged main caught the dev server phoning home, and the agent stopped instead of widening the allowlist
incidents.rule: When a new observer denies traffic on the unchanged base, stop and report; never widen the allowlist, and key any refinement to recorded listeners.
incidents.signature: A new network observer denies connects that the unchanged product already makes.

incidents.title: A preload flag on the package manager argv would not reach the exec'd child processes
incidents.rule: Carry an instrumentation preload through a harness-built environment value that replaces any inherited one, and require a ready record from every process in the tree.
incidents.signature: An instrumentation flag set on a parent command does not reach children that the parent execs.

incidents.title: A merge check rejected a generated migration for whitespace that every earlier generated migration also had
incidents.rule: Do not hand-edit generated files to satisfy a whitespace check; exempt them by an exact pattern and keep checking all other files.
incidents.signature: A whitespace check rejects the output of a code generator.

incidents.title: A second request for a part-row driver showed that the row runner needs a case filter
incidents.rule: A second request for a part-row driver means the runner needs a case filter; until it has one, ask for each sanction.
incidents.signature: A runner cannot run one case, so people ask for private drivers.

incidents.title: A run wrapper exited zero although one of its steps exited one
incidents.rule: Never judge a multi-step run by the wrapper exit status; read the step file and the per-tier counts.
incidents.signature: The wrapper exit status is zero while a recorded step failed.

incidents.title: Heading times in several rulings and briefs ran thirty to seventy minutes ahead of the real clock
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing a timestamp; when a stamp is wrong, trust file and log times and append a correction.
incidents.signature: A heading time was written from memory or estimation, not read from the clock.

incidents.title: A feature branch merged on static gates only, and a unit test elsewhere that encoded the old seed order then went red on main
incidents.rule: A branch that changes product code merges only after a whole-unit comparison equal to the frozen baseline.
incidents.signature: A branch that changes product code passes type, lint, identity and backlog checks, but no whole-unit comparison ran.

incidents.title: Denying unexplained loopback connects in an egress observer broke the app, and the agent stopped instead of widening
incidents.rule: Do not widen an egress allowlist to make the app work; attribute each listener by an operating system query, and allow only listeners owned by instrumented processes.
incidents.signature: A strict denial rule blocks connects the application makes to its own native listeners.

incidents.title: Two lead rulings narrated facts that git disagreed with, and the corrections were appended after checking git
incidents.rule: Before stating a branch base or a new file in a ruling, read it from git; correct by an appended note.
incidents.signature: A ruling states a branch base or a new file that the commit history contradicts.

incidents.title: A pre-action zero-count check in a browser test showed the error selector already matched one element before any action
incidents.rule: Assert that an error selector matches nothing before the action; otherwise a post-action visibility check can pass for the wrong reason.
incidents.signature: The error-visible selector matches an element before the action under test.

incidents.title: A brief said one sorted line for a root with two specs, which could be read two ways
incidents.rule: When a brief and a file header disagree on a count, ask for the unit before editing.
incidents.signature: A count in a brief does not say what it counts.

incidents.title: Teammate replies stopped reaching the lead for about 25 minutes while their files landed on disk
incidents.rule: When a teammate shows finished with no reply, read its report file at once; do not wait for the message.
incidents.signature: A teammate is finished and its files exist, but no reply message arrives.

incidents.title: Two mutation drivers stopped before the restored green because they matched a log-tail string the harness does not print
incidents.rule: A mutation driver must judge exit codes, not log tails; if text must be matched, strip escapes for matching only.
incidents.signature: A driver waits for a text in a log tail, and the text is never printed or is colored.

incidents.title: A lock design passed its own 14 tests, and a reviewer's four forced interleavings each broke it
incidents.rule: A lock or queue needs tests that force a signal or cancel between every pair of publication steps; publish ownership atomically and only when complete.
incidents.signature: Tests of the happy paths pass, and timing between two steps of publication is untested.

incidents.title: A reviewer tested a proposed supersession line with the real checker and found it in the wrong form for an already active predecessor
incidents.rule: Test a proposed replacement marker with the real checker, and use the form that matches the predecessor state.
incidents.signature: A replacement marker is written in the form for a pending predecessor when the predecessor is already active.

incidents.title: An exact list in a test was authored on an older base and reviewed on a newer one where a new collection already existed
incidents.rule: A review of an exact list compares it with the current main product source, including business items, not the internal entries alone.
incidents.signature: An exact list of business items is authored before a merge that adds an item, and reviewed after.

incidents.title: Not visible was the wrong oracle for a collapsed sidebar, because the closed navigation stays in the page with opacity zero and inert
incidents.rule: Bind a collapsed or open state to the attributes the framework sets, not to a visibility matcher.
incidents.signature: A closed menu is still in the DOM, and the visibility matcher ignores inert and off-screen position.

incidents.title: A broad any-alert selector matched the framework's empty route announcer before any action, and a second whole-document probe found the real refusal messages in toasts
incidents.rule: Before authoring an error oracle, diff the whole document, including shadow roots, and bind the new element to the installed source.
incidents.signature: A union selector matches an empty framework element before the action under test.

incidents.title: A dependency had no switch for a dev-only outbound call, and the implementer stopped instead of guessing
incidents.rule: Do not patch a dependency or mask fetch to silence a dev-only call; find which mode reaches it, and place the zero-outbound check where the shipped app runs.
incidents.signature: A requirement to disable an outbound call has no switch in the installed dependency.

incidents.title: A brief named the revision id as the row, and the row runner refused before any test ran
incidents.rule: A runner selection error before any test is not run, never a red; briefs name the base row.
incidents.signature: A runner receives a revision id where it expects the base row name.

incidents.title: A landing helper treated a top-level file name with no slash as a test root, so it copied nothing for it
incidents.rule: A helper that classifies arguments by shape must treat a name with a dot or a slash as a file and must stop when an argument copies nothing.
incidents.signature: A helper classifies an argument by its shape, and a plain file name falls into the wrong class.

incidents.title: A unit row passed only because the caller exported a scratch media directory, and the runner did not own one
incidents.rule: A runner must own the scratch directories its tests write to and ignore caller values for that tier; a row that passes only with an exported path is not green.
incidents.signature: A row passes only when the caller environment supplies a path the runner should own.

incidents.title: An exception that allowed two known failures in a unit comparison was closed the moment their fix merged
incidents.rule: An exception for known failures must end when its fix merges; require the tree to contain the fix and compare to the frozen set.
incidents.signature: A comparison exception outlives the failures it was written for.

incidents.title: A lock protected by an advisory lock on a file opened by path let two holders run when the file was replaced
incidents.rule: After taking a lock on a file opened by path, compare the open file identity with the path identity and retry on mismatch; never create a silent new guard.
incidents.signature: A guard file is unlinked and recreated, and the next caller locks a new file object.

incidents.title: A waiter whose helper could not open its guard spun to the wait limit with tracebacks, and a malformed owner record was skipped silently
incidents.rule: When a guard or an owner identity cannot be proved, exit promptly with a manual step naming the exact path; never spin or skip silently.
incidents.signature: A failure to open the guard and an unreadable owner record produce no report that names a manual step.

incidents.title: A release removed a lock link by owner text without checking that the link pointed at the caller's own stage
incidents.rule: A release removes a lock only after proving, under the guard, that the lock target is the caller's own recorded stage.
incidents.signature: A release compares text and removes a link that may now belong to another holder.

incidents.title: A reviewer's original race script could not run unmodified against the revision because the step it interrupted no longer exists, and the reviewer reported it as stale test semantics
incidents.rule: When an old reproducer cannot run against a revision, report it as stale test semantics, not a kill, and report the adapted run separately.
incidents.signature: An old reproducer asserts a step that the revision removed.

incidents.title: The only copies of eight reviewed drafts sat untracked in one worktree, and the ruling kept them untouched
incidents.rule: Before cleaning a worktree, triage its untracked items against main; keep untouched any item nothing supersedes.
incidents.signature: Reviewed work exists only as untracked files in a worktree that someone may clean.

incidents.title: A full acceptance run stopped at a step hang limit with every reported case passing, and the budget was raised from measured times
incidents.rule: When a step stops at its hang limit with all reported cases passing, do not call it green or red and do not rerun into the same limit; raise the budget from measured times, cite them, then rerun.
incidents.signature: A step stops at its hang limit after a partial report in which every case passed, and the wrapper exits 0.

incidents.title: A triage showed a neighbouring step already at 69 percent of its limit at lower load, so the budget ruling covered it before it failed
incidents.rule: When raising one step budget for load slowdown, check each sibling step's measured share of its limit and cover any that would fail at that slowdown in the same ruling.
incidents.signature: A step that passed in an earlier run used most of its hang limit at lower load than the run that failed.

incidents.title: A static triage found four open rows already done by named merges, and the freeze rule kept them open with the merge commit in the status text
incidents.rule: When a freeze keeps a finished row open, record the delivering merge commit in its status text.
incidents.signature: Plan rows read as open although merged work already delivered them.

incidents.title: A packet author who could not read the rulings file marked every claim resting on it, so the recheck knew what to verify
incidents.rule: When you cannot read a source, mark every claim that rests on it so the next checker knows what to verify.
incidents.signature: A packet states ruling-dependent facts that its author could not check against the source.

incidents.title: A successor draft named as its old bytes a revision that was never approved, so it cannot land against the bytes on main
incidents.rule: Before landing a successor, check that its named old bytes equal the bytes on main; if they name an unapproved revision, park it.
incidents.signature: A successor line names old bytes that differ from the helper actually on main.
